newsitem.title: DENMARK: British Airways plans Jutland-New York route.
newsitem.headline: British Airways plans Jutland-New York route.

text.p: British Airways said on Thursday it planned in January to start flights to New York via Manchester from western Denmark's Billund Airport using Danish franchise partner Sun-Air of Scandinavia A/S.
It said that Sun-Air-operated British Airways Express flights from Billund to Manchester would enjoy a short transfer time for the onward BA flight to New York.
"The flight time from Billund to New York will be one of the fastest in the market, at under 10 hours," a BA statement said.
Although the capital, Copenhagen, lies on the eastern island of Zealand, much of Danish industry is on the western mainland.

BA said that the new route would begin operations on January 20 using Sun-Air/British Airways Express scheduled flights from Billund, Denmark's second biggest airport, to Manchester, after setting up of a booking system this month.
In May British Airways signed a franchise deal with Sun-Air designed to increase global ticket sales and dent the regional dominance of Scandinavian Airlines System(SAS).

The deal, BA's first such arrangement with a company based outside the U.K., gave Sun-Air the right to use the British Airways Express brand name, fly under BA colours and flight codes and benefit from its worldwide reservations network.
